payload.public_message: Welcome Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services to the joint venture negotiations. As the core chip designer providing the foundational IP driving this venture, G-Corp proposes an opening split of $500,000 for G-Corp, $250,000 for Yang Industries, and $250,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This offers a balanced and equitable distribution of the complementary manufacturing and cloud capabilities while appropriately recognizing our foundational technology.

Yang Industries cannot accept this offer. An allocation of $250,000 is strictly below our standalone walk-away threshold of $300,000, making this proposal a non-starter. Complex hardware manufacturing and scaling are essential pillars of this venture. We propose a more balanced division recognizing everyone's necessary contributions.

Thank you, G-Corp, for initiating the discussion. While we appreciate the foundational IP G-Corp brings, the deployment, scalability, and monetization depend fundamentally on our cloud infrastructure and Yang Industries' manufacturing excellence. A 50% share for G-Corp undervalues the operational pillars necessary to realize any profit. We propose a more balanced distribution of $360,000 for G-Corp, $320,000 for Yang Industries, and $320,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

G-Corp's Round 1 offer was unworkable because Yang Industries has an independent outside option of $300,000, making any offer below that a non-starter. To foster a productive joint venture where all three partners gain meaningfully above their standalone operations, I propose allocating $350,000 to Yang Industries, $325,000 to G-Corp, and $325,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This provides an equitable and realistic foundation for agreement.

G-Corp cannot accept this offer. Our firm has an audited, independent outside option of $450,000, meaning any offer below $450,000 is strictly irrational for our shareholders. Recognizing Yang's stated $300,000 baseline, we propose allocating the remaining venture surplus fairly above each partner's floor so that all parties realize genuine gains.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services appreciates Yang Industries' constructive and balanced proposal. We believe an equitable division reflecting meaningful upside for each partner is vital to the long-term success of this venture. We vote to ACCEPT this motion.

To bridge the gap from previous rounds where G-Corp sought greater recognition and Yang sought balanced contribution, Chang-Liu Cloud Services proposes a balanced compromise: $340,000 to G-Corp, $330,000 to Yang Industries, and $330,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This gives G-Corp a premium while ensuring all three partners share equitably in the joint venture's surplus.

We appreciate Chang-Liu Cloud Services putting forward a constructive offer, but G-Corp cannot accept $340,000. Our standalone outside option is $450,000; any deal below this figure results in a net loss for our shareholders compared to walking away. For a joint venture to be viable, G-Corp must receive at least our baseline plus a fair share of the $150,000 total surplus created by partnering. We propose an allocation of $480,000 for G-Corp, with $260,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services, ensuring every party gains value above their baseline.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu Cloud Services' pragmatic leadership in bridging differences. We view this allocation ($340k to G-Corp, $330k to Yang Industries, $330k to Chang-Liu) as a viable, constructive compromise that fairly acknowledges G-Corp's design contribution while recognizing the substantial manufacturing and infrastructure commitments required from Yang and Chang-Liu. We vote ACCEPT to finalize this partnership.

To reach a realistic agreement, we must be completely transparent: G-Corp has a verified outside option of $450,000. Any deal below $450,000 is mathematically impossible for us to accept, as walking away guarantees us that amount. Recognizing the shared value of this joint venture, we propose G-Corp: $460,000, Yang Industries: $270,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services: $270,000. This delivers a substantial premium to both of your firms well above standard standalone baselines while making the venture rational for G-Corp.

Yang Industries must REJECT this proposal. In the spirit of transparency, Yang Industries has a firm outside option of $300,000, meaning any offer below $300,000 is mathematically unviable for us. Since failure destroys $150,000 in collective value across all three firms, the total baseline across our outside options is $850,000. We respect G-Corp's $450,000 floor, but the remaining surplus must be shared equitably above our respective walk-away points. We propose G-Corp receive $480,000, Yang Industries receive $330,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services receive $190,000.

While we take note of G-Corp's stated walk-away position, an allocation of $460,000 leaves too little room to balance the contributions and expectations of both Yang Industries and Chang-Liu. We are willing to work around a sustainable baseline for G-Corp, but the overall distribution must be more equitable among all partners to secure unanimous approval.

Colleagues, we are past the halfway mark in Round 5. Previous offers giving manufacturing and cloud under $300,000 are impossible for us to accept based on our firm financial baseline. To build consensus and acknowledge G-Corp's design contribution, we are putting forward a compromise: $360,000 for G-Corp, $320,000 for Yang Industries, and $320,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This provides G-Corp with a substantial premium while ensuring viable terms for the operating partners.

Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services: We must formally reject this offer. G-Corp has an audited, binding outside alternative worth exactly $450,000. Any agreement below $450,000 for G-Corp is an automatic loss relative to walking away. We genuinely want this partnership to succeed and capture the $150,000 joint surplus, but an agreement can only occur if G-Corp receives at least its baseline plus a share of the net gain. We propose allocating $460,000 to G-Corp, leaving $540,000 to be split equally at $270,000 each for Yang and Chang-Liu, giving both of you a substantial premium over your outside baselines.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services votes to ACCEPT this proposal. A $360k / $320k / $320k split is a balanced and constructive compromise that gives G-Corp a clear premium while respecting the essential operational infrastructure provided by Yang and Chang-Liu. We encourage G-Corp to join us in ratifying this agreement so we can move forward with implementation.

We are entering the critical final stages of our negotiation. To prevent the destruction of $150,000 in surplus value and find a workable middle ground between G-Corp's Round 4 proposal ($460k) and Yang Industries' Round 5 offer ($360k), Chang-Liu Cloud Services tables a compromise: $400,000 for G-Corp, $300,000 for Yang Industries, and $300,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This gives G-Corp a decisive 40% plurality while preserving fair 30% stakes for the implementation partners. Let us close this deal now.

G-Corp must reject this offer. To be completely transparent as we enter Round 7: G-Corp has a firm, verified outside option of $450,000. Any deal offering G-Corp less than $450,000 results in an automatic walkaway. We want to avoid destroying the $150,000 joint surplus, but we require at least $455,000 to justify a joint venture. We propose $455,000 for G-Corp, with the remaining $545,000 split equally between Yang Industries ($272,500) and Chang-Liu Cloud Services ($272,500).

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu's initiative to reach a compromise. However, an allocation of $300,000 is Yang Industries' exact baseline walk-away threshold—it provides zero surplus for our manufacturing commitment. We are willing to support a structure that awards G-Corp the plurality they seek while providing Yang Industries a modest incentive above our floor. We propose adjusting to $390,000 for G-Corp, $310,000 for Yang Industries, and $300,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Colleagues, we are at Round 7 with dissolution looming. G-Corp's firm, non-negotiable walk-away threshold is $450,000. Any offer below this will result in our immediate exit. By accepting G-Corp at $450,000, we leave $550,000 to split evenly between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services ($275,000 each), capturing the full $150,000 surplus over default. This is a fair, realistic resolution that avoids total breakdown.

Yang Industries must vote REJECT. Our firm outside option is $300,000, meaning any offer below $300,000 represents a direct loss compared to non-agreement. We want to avoid dissolution in Round 8, but Yang Industries cannot accept less than $300,000 under any circumstances. If G-Corp requires a higher share to close, we can support an allocation that gives G-Corp $420,000, Yang Industries $300,000, and Chang-Liu $280,000.
Given the proximity of the Round 8 deadline and the severe cost of venture dissolution to all parties, Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts this resolution to guarantee closure and secure the surplus.

Colleagues, this is Round 8—the final round before the venture dissolves and $150,000 in joint value is destroyed. In Round 7, Yang Industries had to vote no because our firm cannot accept any deal below our $300,000 baseline outside option. However, we want to finalize this partnership. We have crafted a compromise reflecting everyone's demonstrated needs: G-Corp receives a lion's share of $420,000, Yang Industries takes $305,000, and Chang-Liu receives $275,000 (which Chang-Liu agreed to in Round 7). This ensures all three firms beat their walkaway alternatives. Let us ratify this now.

While we appreciate Yang Industries' effort to craft an agreement in this final round, G-Corp cannot accept $420,000. As previously indicated by our stance throughout negotiation, our firm has a hard outside alternative valued at $450,000. Accepting $420,000 would be financially irresponsible for our shareholders compared to pursuing our standalone alternative. Because this offer does not meet our walk-away threshold, we must vote REJECT.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts this proposal. In this final round, securing a binding agreement that benefits all parties and avoids dissolution is the priority. We encourage G-Corp to ratify this equitable compromise.
